## Verdict: FAIL — one failing line (a new blocker); N-53 (1) itself is fixed

N-53 (1) is fixed. The two-line fix is in place, and the item's other owns have no second instance. The P1 pins fail
on the old line and pass on the fix. All ten ruling seeds replay without a throw, and every targeted mutant is killed
except one equivalent. No seed that never grew inside a split changes its result. All gates are green.

The item fails on one NEW finding, and it is a blocker under N-45 (a): a wrong result on an honest input. A lawful
`splitThrough` on a §3.10-valid arena commits through `tx()` an arena that breaches §3.10's hard clearance invariant.
This is the open case the round's author recorded as C-0279 (4) and "routed to the session". No ruling, fix-round
entry or KNOWN-ISSUES row for it exists in `checks/M0-spec-notes.md`, `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` or the checks folder
(grep for `C-0279` and `one-ring exemption`: only the choices row). N-53 (7) requires such a report to be routed when
it is written. N-45 (a) and N-53 both say a silently wrong committed result is never a KI.

### Failing line F-1 — a split commits a §3.10 clearance breach (C-0279 (4)), CONFIRMED

* **What happens.** When `splitThrough` splits a sub-edge s–t at v, s and t stop being neighbours. The edges at t are
  then no longer in s's one-ring, and the edges at s are no longer in t's. §3.10 row "clearance" says every vertex lies
  at least `minEdge` from every edge outside its one-ring. §3.6's placement rule (iii) checks only the new vertex and
  its incident edges. The commit's clearance row checks only new, placed and moved vertices and their incident edges.
  So when s stands within `minEdge` of an edge at t, the breach commits. This happens on a chord meeting the frame at a
  shallow angle (6.6° – 8° in the cases below, all above `minFaceAngle` 5°).
* **Evidence.** The checker's own probe is `packages/kernel/test/insert/zzchk/clear.test.ts`, run in the mirror on the
  fixed `splitThrough.ts`. It builds 300 chord arenas (`chordSpec`, generator `0xc1ea + seed`) and makes 40 random L1
  splits on each. It runs `problems()` (support.ts, the §3.10 validator) before and after every split. The first
  breaching split of a seed is then replayed on a fresh arena with the same history, as a `tx()` callback batch at L1.
  * Bare arenas: `seeds 300, splits 11678, seeds with a breach 17, tx replays 17, committed with breach 0`. All 17
    were refused, but for an unrelated reason: `E_INVARIANT: an edge's birth level L1 is not the lowest level among its
    rows (L5)`. A bare edge carries no row.
  * Role-dressed arenas (`ROLES=1`: `margin` on L0 edges, `way` on L1, as real arenas carry):
    `seeds 300, splits 11678, seeds with a breach 17, tx replays 17, committed with breach 17`. For example, seed 6 splits
    (2912, 3984)–(3034, 4000) at (2966, 3996) and gives v (2967, 3991). The probe printed
    `before=0 problems; COMMITTED; after=1: vertex (2912, 3984) stands within minEdge of edge (3034, 4000)–(0, 4000)`.
    Seed 34 gives `vertex (2003, 23) stands within minEdge of edge (0, 0)–(2168, 0)`, and seed 40 gives
    `vertex (3981, 2702) stands within minEdge of edge (4000, 2539)–(4000, 4000)`.
  * This agrees with the author's own record. C-0279 (4) reports 29 of 1 000 seeds and 10 `tx()` commits.
* **Why it is a blocker and not a KI.** The input is lawful: a §3.10-valid arena, a corner above `minFaceAngle`, and a
  point on the edge. The result is committed (no refusal, no warning) and breaks a hard §3.10 invariant. That is
  N-45 (a)'s "silently wrong committed result", the brief's "wrong result on an honest input", and N-44 (2)'s "a result
  is committed only if it keeps every bar checked at commit". The defect is old. It dates from the item's first
  landing, not from this round's fix, but no earlier check found it.
* **Required change.** The session rules on the owner first, because both candidate fixes sit on a design gap and
  shift rates measured under N-44. The candidates are:
  1. M0-a-04's placement rule (iii) also checks s against the edges at t and t against the edges at s. A split where
     every candidate fails falls back onto the nearer endpoint (detect-and-refuse in placement terms, N-45's
     preference).
  2. The split journals s and t for the commit's clearance row (M0-a-06's), so `tx()` refuses the batch.

  Either way, add a pin: one of the probe's cases (for example seed 6, role-dressed, as a `tx()` callback) must be
  refused or placed clear, never committed with a breach. Also extend the step 1-2 B-FUZZ to run sequences of
  splits on near-frame chords with `problems()` after each. Then state the one-time shift in placement and refusal
  counts, including any shift in M0-a-05's measured insertChain caps.

## (1) The previous failing line — N-53 (1): FIXED (CONFIRMED)

  `allocVertex` and `allocEdgePair`. It takes `const T = p.halfEdges` after `allocEdgePair`, with the comment naming
  the doubling. `O = T.origin` (line 304) and every splice write (264 – 280) use the live table. `p.vertices` is read
  live after the allocations (281 – 282, 302 – 303). `p.roles` is one object whose columns `growRoleRows` reassigns,
  so `R.kind[r]` reads live. Diff against the pre-fix copy: exactly the two lines.
